title: Bold Dome Huggies
concept: A sheet of clear bubble wrap on a flat pastel lilac ground, the pair of polished dome huggies sitting among the bubbles, domes echoing domes; one popped bubble.
headline: Don't pop these.
prop: sheet of clear small bubble wrap on flat pastel lilac paper
notes: PASS (8.2), attempt 2. Near-overhead flat lay: the bubble wrap's straight cut edge crosses at 0.27, so the top 27% is plain pastel lilac paper (calm for a headline, either top corner). One hoop lies face up as a gold O (0.40-0.585), the other tipped on its side lower right (0.60-0.76), showing the dome swelling to the bottom and tapering to the thin snap bar; hinge bar, hairline seam, plain mirror polish, warm yellow gold. Scale: the face-up hoop is about 1.85 bubbles wide, so it reads about 18mm against the 10mm bubbles (true 16mm), within tolerance. Doubts: the popped bubble (right of the face-up hoop) is subtle at phone size because every bubble carries crinkle highlights; the lying hoop's lower edge picks up a soft rosy lilac reflection. Not a face: the two hoops are staggered and read differently (O and crescent). Attempt 1 (7.5) was the richer picture with a clearly popped bubble, but its hoops were 2.2 bubbles wide (about 22mm, 1.4x too big).
prompt: Vertical 9:16 playful editorial advertising photograph for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand, a three-quarter macro still life looking down at about 45 degrees: a pair of polished gold dome huggie hoops sitting among the clear bubbles of a sheet of bubble wrap on a flat pastel lilac paper ground, domes echoing domes. IMAGE 1 is our approved product photograph of this exact pair and the authority on it: its construction, size, metal colour and finish; ignore its background, its plaster block and its light. COUNTABLE FACTS: 2 hoops, 0 stones. Each hoop is 16mm across, a chunky rounded dome tube that swells to about 6mm thick at the bottom and tapers to a slim hinged snap bar about 2mm thick at the top; its outer face is plain mirror-polished with no texture, no engraving and no stones; one fine hairline seam marks the hinge at the side. Warm yellow 18k gold tone, never rose gold or copper, even where it reflects the lilac. The hoop must stay a smooth dome that swells at the bottom and tapers to the hinge, never an even round tube, never a thin wire hoop, never a large hoop, never twisted, ribbed or textured; both hoops stay closed. Scale test, and the fault this frame fixes: the previous attempt drew each hoop more than two bubbles wide, so it read as a 22mm hoop; this time each hoop is only about one and a half bubbles wide, never two. This is ordinary small bubble wrap whose round bubbles are each 10mm across and 4mm tall, set in a neat grid, and the camera sits a little further back so that about eight bubbles fit across the width of the frame; each hoop is 16mm across, barely wider than one bubble and a half, and its 6mm-thick swollen bottom is only about half a bubble wide. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the bubbles; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged. Scene: one sheet of clear bubble wrap lies across the middle and lower part of the frame on flat pastel lilac paper, its straight cut top edge running across at about one third of the frame height, so the top quarter of the frame is plain, calm, empty lilac paper for a headline. The two hoops sit in the middle band of the frame, never side by side and never at the same height: one hoop stands upright on its thick swollen bottom, nestled in the valley between bubbles, seen almost face-on as a round gold O; the second hoop lies tipped over on its side about 3cm lower and to the right, seen in profile as a fat gold crescent that shows how the dome swells and tapers. Right beside the upright hoop, one bubble has been popped: flattened, crinkled, creased clear plastic, the joke of the frame. The bubbles are crystal clear, each with a tiny bright highlight, tinted lilac by the paper below, with soft lilac shadows; each hoop casts a small crisp contact shadow on the plastic, which dimples slightly under the upright hoop. Light: one soft large key light from the upper left, giving gentle clean light and one soft natural shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right on the metal, so each polished dome shows a crisp bright white streak along its swell and a dark rolled edge on the inside of the curve, with mirror reflections of the lilac and the bubbles in the gold. Honest macro optics: the two hoops and the bubbles round them needle-sharp, the far bubbles falling gently soft. Real texture: the slight wrinkle of the plastic film, the matte paper grain, natural film grain. title: Baguette Halo Drops
concept: Close among the crystal drops of an antique gilt chandelier; the pair of earrings hangs from the chandelier's brass pins among the crystals as if two more drops, warm candle glow above.
headline: Off the chandelier.
prop: antique gilt-brass chandelier with clear octagon bead festoons and long faceted prisms
notes: FLAGGED at 7.5, the better of two attempts, kept under the 7.5 rule; neither reached 8. Gilt chandelier against a deep aubergine wall: the two earrings hang among octagon-bead festoons and long faceted prisms, staggered (left 0.31-0.565, right 0.52-0.76, turned three-quarter), not a face. Construction exact at full size: polished gold rim, ring of slim baguette rays with gold beads outside and a beaded gold ring inside, 5mm centre pearl in a gold collar with its little cross-bars, short loop and cap holding one round 10mm drop pearl; warm yellow gold. Scale doubt (the fault): each disc is about 1.44x the width of an octagon bead and each earring about 0.6 of a prism's length, so it reads roughly 1.4x its true 14mm disc / 26mm length against typical chandelier crystals. Other doubts: the left earring's hanging pin is not visible (it reads as resting against the festoon), one small lens-star glint on the right rim, a cream candle sleeve in the top-left corner (top-right is calm aubergine for the headline). Attempt 1 (7.0): same exact construction, but the discs were 1.55x the octagon beads and the candle sleeves and bulbs filled the top quarter.

title: Prism Cluster Studs
concept: A clear glass sweet jar of jelly beans in purple, pink and yellow, lid off; the pair of studs sits on the jar's rim, every stone matching a bean.
headline: Not for eating.
prop: clear glass sweet jar of purple, pink and yellow jelly beans on sage green
notes: EMPTY: no attempt reached 7.5. Best was attempt 1 (6.5; copy_space, subject_y and tone describe it): a low shot of a glass jar of purple, pink and yellow jelly beans on sage green, one stud on the front of the rim and one further round, a pink bean between them, calm sage top quarter. Stone order exact (purple, pink, yellow, purple, pink; mirror pair; tiny pearls) but each stud is about two jelly beans long, about 40mm against a true 20mm: a 2x scale fail. Attempt 2 (5.5) named the fault; the studs came out about 1.55 beans long, stood vertically against the outside of the glass instead of on the rim (implausible), faced each other like brackets either side of the pink bean, and had the stone order wrong (purple, pink, yellow, pink, purple) with oversized pearls; yellow beans drifted to orange. A third try should drop the jar close-up for a wider frame with the studs among loose beans on a flat ground, where the bean referent is unambiguous.
prompt: Vertical 9:16 candy-bright editorial advertising photograph for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand, a low three-quarter close-up of the rim of a glass sweet jar: a pair of silver cluster stud earrings resting on the rim of an open jar of jelly beans in exactly their colours, purple, pink and yellow. IMAGE 2 is a close-up of one stud for construction detail only (the stone order, the claws and the tiny pearls); ignore its size and framing. COUNTABLE FACTS: 2 studs, mirror images of each other, 10 coloured stones in all. Each stud is a gentle smiling arc about 20mm long of exactly 5 coloured cubic zirconia in bright silver claws, in this order from one end of the arc to the other: 1 violet-purple square princess cut tilted on its point, 1 soft baby-pink baguette leaning, 1 larger golden-yellow emerald cut standing upright at the centre (the largest stone, about 6mm tall), 1 violet-purple princess cut tilted on its point, 1 soft pink baguette leaning; 8 tiny round white pearls about 2.5mm tucked into the gaps around the stones, each held by small silver beads. Bright cool rhodium silver tone. Exactly 5 coloured stones per stud in the order purple, pink, yellow, purple, pink, never a sixth colour such as blue or green; the yellow emerald cut stays the largest stone, at the centre; the pearls stay tiny, never as large as a coloured stone; the metal stays bright silver, never gold. Scale test: a jelly bean is about 20mm long and 13mm wide; each stud is an arc about 20mm long, exactly the length of one jelly bean, and its yellow centre stone, the largest, is about 6mm tall, half a bean's width; the tiny pearls are far smaller than a bean. The jar is about 11cm across. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the jelly beans; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged. Scene: a heavy, plain, clear glass apothecary sweet jar, lid off and out of frame, filled to the brim with glossy jelly beans in only three colours, violet-purple, baby pink and golden yellow, stands on a flat soft sage-green surface against a matching plain sage-green wall. The jar has a thick, flat, polished glass rim about 8mm wide. The camera is close and just above rim height, so the rim is a shallow ellipse across the middle of the frame with the heaped beans just behind it. One stud lies face up on the front of the rim, following its curve, nearest the camera and sharpest; the second lies further round the rim to the right, turned at a different angle and slightly foreshortened, never side by side with the first; one single pink jelly bean lies on the rim between them, the same length as each stud. A few loose beans have spilled onto the sage surface at the foot of the jar. The joke reads in one glance: the brightest sweets on the rim are not for eating. Through the glass the beans below show soft refraction. The top quarter of the frame is plain, calm sage-green wall, empty for a headline. Light: one soft large key light from the upper left with one soft natural shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right on the metal, so the bright silver claws show crisp white edges and dark rolled edges, and every coloured stone carries internal sparkle and one pure-white catchlight; the jelly beans have a glossy sugar-shell sheen.
